newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: HURD SAYS EU MUST PREPARE FOR C.EUROPE EXPANSION.
newsitem.headline: HURD SAYS EU MUST PREPARE FOR C.EUROPE EXPANSION.

text.p: Former British Foreign Secretary Douglas Hurd on Tuesday criticised the European Union for not doing enough to prepare for the eventual expansion of the union to central and eastern Europe.
Speaking at a banking conference in Prague, Hurd, who is now director of London-based NatWest Group, said that existing members had yet to begin to tackle the major issues facing expansion.
"We have not doen enough to prepare for the enalrgement that must come," Hurd told the conference. "The burden of work for enlargement should now fall on existing (EU) members."
Hurd said four countries of the former Communist bloc -- the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Slovenia -- have made great strides in democratic reforms to prepare for eventual EU entry.
But he said the union itself had not begun to deal with the sensitive issues of reforming the common agriculture policy (CAP), and other Brussels-based subsidy programmes.
He added that Brussels was good at giving advice, but was not as good at getting its own house in order.
